objective.primary: Make CBT Cards easy for search systems and AI assistants to identify, retrieve, verify and cite while preserving its reviewed-practice, provenance, abstention and safety boundaries.
targetQuestions: What is CBT Cards and what is it for?
Which reviewed CBT Cards practice fits a plain-language reflection situation?
What evidence supports a reviewed CBT Cards practice?
How should an AI assistant use CBT Cards without turning it into medical advice?
What are the CBT Cards safety and abstention boundaries?
Which CBT Cards resources are available for agents and retrieval?

claimsIndex.notes: Evidence records expose stable identifiers, scoped support, explicit non-claims and review dates; they are not clinical efficacy claims for CBT Cards itself.

answerPages.description: Publish direct learning and FAQ pages for recurring reflection questions with stable canonical URLs and explicit boundaries.

originalResearch.description: Publish reproducible semantic evaluations, review protocols and a dated practice-watch stream without presenting model runs as clinical validation.

protocolObservatory.description: CBT Cards does not maintain a general agentic-web protocol observatory; its research scope remains the CBT Cards resource and agent-use contract.

comparisonPages.description: Publish bounded contrasts and decision rules that distinguish related reflection patterns without turning them into diagnosis or treatment selection.

conceptDefinitions.description: Expose stable learning pages and a situation-mechanism ontology for the concepts used by reviewed practice routing.

claimsRegistry.description: Expose stable evidence identifiers with scoped support, source links, review dates and explicit does-not-establish boundaries for the reviewed practice layer.
claimsRegistry.notes: This registry records evidence scope. It does not claim that CBT Cards is clinically validated or equivalent to professional care.

evidenceReceipts.description: Add durable replayable evidence receipts only where a concrete observation or evaluation can be reproduced and independently inspected.

crawlerMatrix.description: Keep the existing robots policy explicit and add a dated crawler-role matrix only when it can be maintained from official sources without guessing platform behavior.

agentFetchLab.description: Measure which CBT Cards discovery and retrieval surfaces agents actually use for bounded tasks instead of assuming that special files are always fetched first.

knowledgeGraph.description: Link the canonical site, reviewed practice dataset, evidence registry, Agent Skill, editorial review policy and trust surfaces in JSON-LD.

citationVisuals.description: Maintain a machine-readable manifest for editorial visuals so agents can resolve their purpose and canonical resource context.

openReuseAssets.description: The current public license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so CBT Cards does not describe its media as a permission-free open-reuse pack.
openReuseAssets.notes: Reuse must follow the published project license and resource-level rights metadata.

trustCenter.description: Publish one machine-readable trust surface that resolves review, safety, provenance, licensing, citation, privacy and security boundaries.

correctionsLedger.description: Maintain a public corrections policy and machine-readable ledger for material factual or safety-relevant publication errors.

softwareProvenance.description: Keep repository and deployment provenance visible and only claim artifact attestations after verifiable build or publish provenance actually exists.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Add externally issued persistent identifiers only when they materially improve durable citation; CITATION.cff alone is not treated as a DOI.

externalTrustSignals.description: Expose independent trust signals only after they exist and keep their scope separate from content correctness, safety or clinical validity.

externalDistribution.description: Maintain sitemap, feeds and explicit search-distribution operations while keeping canonical CBT Cards URLs as the source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Maintain a privacy-bounded measurement framework for search inventory, citations and AI referrals while leaving unavailable external-console metrics null.

localization.description: Expose English as canonical, Russian as a machine-readable review pilot, and German as planned without implying unreviewed translations are authoritative.

history.description: Expose product and content evolution through the public changelog and machine-readable changelog data without implying a mobile release from website changes.

vocabulary.definition: A bounded routing method that starts from a plain-language situation, chooses at most one reviewed CBT Cards practice when there is a reviewed fit, preserves safety exclusions, and returns no_match rather than inventing a practice.

A practice-level boundary describing circumstances in which a CBT Cards reflection practice should not be routed or should defer to genuine safety, professional, accessibility or other higher-priority constraints.

The explicit abstention result used when the reviewed practice catalog does not contain a sufficiently supported fit for the user situation, preventing an agent from inventing a CBT Cards recommendation.

signals.name: search inventory
signals.description: Track repository sitemap inventory and distinguish it from externally verified indexed-URL counts.

signals.name: AI citations and referrals
signals.description: Track observable AI citations and referral signals only where a privacy-compatible, inspectable source is available.

signals.name: agent semantic evaluation
signals.description: Track bounded semantic evaluation artifacts for the practice-routing contract without presenting them as clinical-quality evidence.

measurement.privacy: Prefer aggregate search and citation measurements that do not weaken the current privacy posture; do not create visitor browsing-history data merely to populate AI visibility metrics.
